name: harness-launcher
description: Start or resume an AI coding CLI in a terminal, in exactly the folder you want, with first-class multi-root support.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace the launcher ignores workspace-level commands, arguments and paths, and uses only your user settings.

harness-launcher-rocket.description: Harness Launcher rocket, used by the status bar button.

enumDescriptions: Folder that contains the saved `.code-workspace` file: the hub of a multi-root workspace.
The workspace folder whose Explorer name matches `#harnessLauncher.cwd.folderName#`.
The first folder of the workspace.
The workspace folder that holds the active editor's file.
Ask every time: the hub folder or any workspace folder.
The absolute path in `#harnessLauncher.cwd.path#`.
harnessLauncher.cwd.mode.markdownDescription: Working directory of the new terminal. When the mode cannot resolve (for example `workspaceFile` in a single-folder window), the terminal starts in the first workspace folder, then in your home folder, and a warning names the mode that failed. Set it at **Workspace** level to store the rule inside the `.code-workspace` file, so each hub carries its own.

harnessLauncher.cwd.folderName.markdownDescription: Workspace folder used by the `namedFolder` mode of `#harnessLauncher.cwd.mode#`. Type **the name the VS Code Explorer shows, not the folder name on disk**: in a `.code-workspace` file, a folder entry with `"name": "My Clone"` and `"path": "my-clone"` matches `My Clone`. The match is exact and case-sensitive.

harnessLauncher.cwd.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path used by the `path` mode of `#harnessLauncher.cwd.mode#`. Supports `~`, `${userHome}`, `${workspaceFileDir}`, `${workspaceFolder}` (the first folder) and `${workspaceFolder:<name>}`, where `<name>` is the name the Explorer shows, not the folder name on disk.

enumDescriptions: Terminal panel.
Editor area, as a tab in the active group.
Editor area, in a group beside the active editor.

harnessLauncher.statusBar.enabled.markdownDescription: Show a rocket button in the status bar that opens the launcher. Unlike the editor title button, it stays visible with no file open.

enumDescriptions: Double-click works like a single click: it opens the launcher.
Claude Code.
Codex.
Gemini CLI.
GitHub Copilot.
opencode.
harnessLauncher.quickLaunch.harness.markdownDescription: Harness whose **New session** starts when you double-click a rocket button, in the editor tab row or in the status bar. A single click still opens the launcher, a moment later so a second click can arrive. When the harness is not detected, a double-click opens the launcher instead. A custom harness counts when its `id` replaces a built-in one.

harnessLauncher.customHarnesses.markdownDescription: Extra harnesses, edited in `settings.json`. Each entry is `{ "id", "label", "command", "newArgs", "continueArgs", "resumeArgs" }`; `id` and `command` are required. Without `continueArgs` the harness has no **Continue last session** action. An entry whose `id` matches a built-in harness replaces its label, command and arguments.

id.description: Unique id, also used by the harnessLauncher.launch command.

label.description: Name shown in the launcher and as the terminal name.

command.description: Executable name on PATH, or an absolute path.

continueArgs.description: Arguments for Continue last session. Leave it out when the CLI has no way to jump to its latest session.

enumDescriptions: Show Claude Code when its command is detected (found on PATH and `--version` prints a version).
Always show it, even when it is not detected.
Never show it.
harnessLauncher.claude.enabled.markdownDescription: When the launcher lists Claude Code.

harnessLauncher.claude.command.markdownDescription: Executable for Claude Code: a name looked up on `PATH`, or an absolute path. Put arguments in the arguments settings, not here.

harnessLauncher.claude.newArgs.markdownDescription: Arguments for **New session**. Parsed like a shell: separate with spaces, group with `"double"` or `'single'` quotes. Each argument is passed quoted, never as raw shell text.

harnessLauncher.claude.continueArgs.markdownDescription: Arguments for **Continue last session**. The default `--continue` opens the most recent conversation without the session picker. The launcher hides this action when it matches New or Resume. Parsed like a shell: separate with spaces, group with `"double"` or `'single'` quotes. Each argument is passed quoted, never as raw shell text.

harnessLauncher.claude.resumeArgs.markdownDescription: Arguments for **Resume session**. The default `--resume` opens the session picker. Parsed like a shell: separate with spaces, group with `"double"` or `'single'` quotes. Each argument is passed quoted, never as raw shell text.
